Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the SolaraTech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants are asked to limit themselves to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SolaraTech's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Mike Chen, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. SolaraTech delivered exceptional results in Q3, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance. First, the highly supportive policy and regulatory environment accelerating our growth. Second, our effective tax equity financing and project-level financing strategies. Third, our disciplined capital expenditure and operating expense management. Fourth, strong additions to our development pipeline and achievement of major project milestones. Fifth, significant market trends positively impacting our operations. Sixth, robust trends in our gross and operating margins. And seventh, our prudent debt levels and optimized financing costs.

Now, I'll hand over the call to John Ramirez to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Sarah. Our financial performance in Q3 was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.45 billion, representing a 42% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 31.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $265 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $210 million, or $1.45 per share. We ended the quarter with $950 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

To give more context on these results and the key aspects Sarah mentioned, let me start with the policy and regulatory landscape, which remains a massive tailwind for SolaraTech. As a leader in utility-scale solar PV and energy storage solutions, we're positioned to capitalize on the global shift toward decarbonization. In the US, the Inflation Reduction Act continues to drive benefits, with over $110 billion in clean energy manufacturing investments announced since 2022. Solar module capacity has surged 250% to more than 200 GW by year-end 2024, according to SEIA data. This has boosted our domestic production at Texas and Ohio facilities, qualifying for the full 45Q tax credit stack—base 30% ITC plus 10% domestic content adder and up to 10% for energy communities. In Q3, this yielded an effective 48% tax equity yield on our 2.5 GW portfolio additions, up from 32% pre-IRA. The transferability provisions have unlocked $15 billion in monetized credits sector-wide YTD, and we forecast our share exceeding $500 million in 2025 with 1.2 GW of bifacial TOPCon modules paired with 800 MWh BESS deployments.

Challenges like interconnection queues persist, but FERC Order 2022 prioritizes ready-to-build projects—we've fast-tracked 15 into the fast lane, cutting 18-24 months off timelines. Tariffs on Southeast Asian solar cells at 50-250% AD/CVD rates favor our localization; our US-made n-type HJT modules are 15% ahead for DOE's Solar for All grants, targeting $200 million in low-income deployments next year.

In Europe, REPowerEU and Fit for 55 target 45% renewables by 2030. The Net Zero Industry Act streamlines permitting to under two years for gigafactories—key for our 5 GWh LFP battery plant in Poland, securing €250 million under IPCEI ULTIMATE for solid-state R&D. CBAM from 2026 adds 20-30% premiums on carbon-intensive imports, spiking European PPAs 35% YoY; we've signed 1.8 GW in Germany, Spain, and Italy with offtakers like Uniper and RWE valuing our 25-year shapeable hybrid output. Revised Renewable Energy Directive III boosts hybrid co-location, unlocking 10 GW curtailed wind sites where our 200 MW floating PV in the Netherlands achieves 25% higher capacity factors.

In Asia-Pacific, China's dual carbon goals drive 220 GW solar additions in 2024 per BloombergNEF, with Golden Sun favoring our distributed generation microinverters—up 40% in Japan under GX Promotion Act. India's PLI 2.0 partners us with Adani Green on 3 GW PERC modules via 51% local content. ASEAN grids like Vietnam's PDP8 target 47% renewables—we're bidding 1 GW BESS.

Globally, COP28's renewables tripling sees 50 GW corporate PPAs in 2024, up 25% YoY. Policy outpaces supply chains, so our $1.2 billion capex emphasizes 40% US localization, 30% EU net-zero supply, and AI O&M for <2% curtailment. Risks like elections exist, but bipartisan support endures. This supports 25-30% EBITDA growth to $1.8 billion, 95% free cash flow conversion.

Next, our tax equity financing and project-level financing remain the bedrock of our capital stack. We've deployed over 15 GW since IPO, evolving with IRA tailwinds in a higher-rate world. Tax equity monetizes ITC/PTC attributes—base 30% ITC plus adders. Transferability is key, but partnerships yield better economics: 65-75% costs at 6-8% IRR pre-flip.

In Q3, we closed $520 million tax equity for 800 MW Southwest solar—Gemini expansion and Mojave Dawn with First Solar bifacials and Nextracker. JPMorgan and Goldman provided $300 million. YTD, tax equity funds 68% US capex, up from 55%. Pricing tightened 50 bps, but we protect sponsor IRRs. Piloting in Europe with yieldcos.

Project-level debt is non-recourse atop tax equity in 60/20/20 stacks. Q3: $1.3 billion at 5.8% blended, with 1.45x DSCR on 20-year PPAs. $850 million construction loans from MUFG/Citi for 500 MW/2 GWh Texas BESS stacking 45X credits. $450 million ECA for Midwest wind repower. $200 million green bonds at SOFR +225 bps.

Margins stabilized at SOFR +175-250 bps; hedged 70% to <5.5%. BESS tighter by 50 bps. US 70%, Europe 20%, APAC 10%. WACC 4.2%, down 30 bps QoQ, scaling 25 GW backlog to 35 GW. Initiatives: 45% domestic content, hybrid stacking, 1.3x DSCR stress-tested. Expect $3-4 billion closings in 2025.

Turning to CAPEX and OPEX, we deployed $285 million CAPEX in Q3, YTD $920 million, on track for $1.25-1.35 billion FY—up 22% YoY on IRA/REPowerEU. Solar 52% ($148M): 1.2 GW SunForge TOPCon in Southwest, $45M EPC. Wind 28% ($80M): 400 MW GaleForce. BESS/emerging 20% ($57M): 1.5 GWh VoltVault, iron-air pilot, green H2.

CAPEX/MW $1.1M, down from $1.4M via hedging polysilicon at $18/kg, in-house BOS. Q4 $350-400M, 2025 $1.8-2.0B for 3 GW.

OPEX $162M, flat % rev at 22%, FY $680-710M. O&M $73M ($4.80/MWh, down 7%): AI CleanOps cuts downtime 22%. SG&A $57M (5% YoY growth). R&D/G&A $32M: perovskites, HydroFlex. OPEX/EBITDA 52%, LCOE $28/MWh. Hedged inputs, TechStack saves $50M by 2026.

On gross and operating margins, Q3 GAAP gross 28.5% (up 320 bps YoY), adjusted 29.8%. Op margin 12.3% GAAP, 13.7% adjusted. Polysilicon down 70% YoY to $8/kg, locked $9.50/kg. ASP $0.32/W up 8%, TOPCon 65% mix. Yields 24.8%. US 32.1%, Europe 27.8%, APAC 25.4%.

OpEx $156M (18.2% rev): R&D $42M HJT/BESS, SG&A 10.8%. Q4 gross 29.5-30.5%, op 13-14%. US capex $500M for CdTe.

Finally, debt levels: gross $5.2B (down 8% YoY), net $4.75B, 3.4x leverage. Cost 4.15% (down 50 bps), 85% fixed, 6.8Y maturity. Green bonds SOFR+145 bps. US 65% at 3.9%, Europe 25% 4.8% hedged, APAC 10% 5.2%. Optimization: refinance $800M, hybrids, AI forecasting. FY25 capex 70% non-dilutive.

These elements drive our margins and growth. Now, significant market trends: solar 447 GWdc 2023, 510 GW 2024, LCOE $24/MWh. US IRA pipeline 85 GWac. BESS 115 GWh 2023, 250 GWh 2024. H2 electrolyzers $450/kW. Our shipments 8.2 GWdc Q3, margins 28.5%. SolaraStore 2.8 GWh backlog. Supply stabilization aids.

I'll now turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss our project development activities.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, John. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 28.6 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies—up 22% YoY and 8% QoQ. We categorize: 2.1 GW early, 12.4 GW advanced, 10.5 GW shovel-ready, 3.6 GW construction. Positions us for 4-5 GW annual to construction.

Q3 additions 3.2 GW COD 2027: 1.8 GW solar+storage DesertForge in ERCOT/CAISO with LONGi/Qcells/CATL. 850 MW Horizon Wind repower GE Vernova. 550 MW Electra H2 PEM/alkaline.

Milestones: 17 achieved, 1.4 GW converted. FID Solara Peak 450 MW solar+200 MWh, $650M tax equity, PPA Dominion. Full permitting Atlantic Breeze Offshore 750 MW. PPA Prairie Wind 300 MW Xcel.

Pillars: AI yield +8%, diversification 45% US/30% Europe/25% APAC/LatAm, JV Fluence 2 GWh. Q4 3-4 GW adds. Operator ready, but first to Elena.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Maria. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape, including perovskite tandems and high-efficiency inverters reducing silver use.

Next, Tom Reilly will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Elena. Sustainability is a core value at SolaraTech, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon footprint to near-zero, improving our energy efficiency across operations, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability, aligning with SBTi targets and low-carbon modules at 45 gCO2/kWh.

Now, Mike Chen will provide operational highlights.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Tom. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets—95% fleet availability via CleanOps AI, predictive maintenance, and supply chain resilience. We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed, with O&M at $4.80/MWh.

I'll turn it back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Mike. To summarize, SolaraTech had an exceptional Q3. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your request, press the pound key. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks for the question, Jane. International expansion is a key pillar for SolaraTech, building on our 55% non-US pipeline exposure. We're prioritizing Europe and APAC where policy aligns—REPowerEU grants fund our Poland gigafactory, and India's PLI supports 3 GW with Adani. In Q4, we'll bid 1 GW ASEAN BESS and advance 500 MW Australian floating PV. We'll deploy $400 million capex overseas in 2025, targeting 30% revenue from Europe/APAC via local JVs like Fluence, while mitigating FX with 80% hedged PPAs. This diversifies from US while leveraging IRA learnings globally.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Bob Smith:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Bob. Intermittency is core to our innovation focus. Our hybrid solar-plus-BESS deployments, like 1.8 GW DesertForge with 4-hour LFP at 98% RTE, firm output for 25-year shapeable PPAs. AI-optimized SolaraStore VPP aggregates 2 GWh backlog, stacking arbitrage, capacity, and freq regulation—curtailment <2%. Long-duration pilots like 100 MW/400 MWh iron-air target 100-hour discharge. Grid tech: silicon-carbide inverters boost uptime 5%, integrating with SCADA for duck curve mitigation. This delivers 55%+ capacity factors, outpacing standalone renewables.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

John Ramirez:
Absolutely, Lisa. Subsidies like IRA ITC/PTC stackers—up to 70% with adders—directly lift our unlevered IRRs to 10-12%, contributing ~$500 million to 2025 credits. Section 45X manufacturing yields $45/kWh on US modules/BESS, boosting Q3 gross margins 300 bps to 28.5%. Transferability provides flexibility if tax equity demand softens. Europe REPowerEU grants €250M for Poland; India's PLI 50% subsidies on local content. These de-risk 85% revenue visibility, supporting 25% EBITDA CAGR. Absent them, LCOE rises 20-30%, but bipartisan US/EU support ensures durability through 2030.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Sarah Thompson:
Demand growth is explosive, David—global electrification + AI data centers drive 4-5% CAGR to 2030 per IEA, with US peaking at 10% YoY in ERCOT from hyperscalers. Renewables >40% mix there. Corporates like Google sign 15 GW PPAs YTD for 24/7 clean power. Our 28.6 GW pipeline captures this, with 60% utility/corporate backed. Expect 20% SolaraTech revenue CAGR, prioritizing hybrids for firming—LCOE $25/MWh unsubsidized competitive with gas peakers.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for any closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of SolaraTech. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
